comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: People call the Sahara unlivable, but communities here seem to prove the exact opposite. Maybe ‘harsh’ depends on who’s looking?

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That’s a great observation, @LifewaysTravel. It’s incredible how human resilience redefines what "livable" means, even in the heart of the Sahara. Thanks for the insight!

comments.author: @GrahameMcLeod
comments.text: Nice video. I once spent five weeks there. Great culture. A pity that you did not include Oualata, a real gem; also, Ouadane.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: Five weeks in Mauritania must have been an incredible experience, @GrahameMcLeod! Thank you for the suggestions; Oualata and Ouadane are definitely gems we hope to cover in a future episode.

comments.author: @mmcsm
comments.text: A few images in your video are not from Mauritania, but despite that, it's a very nice film!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We appreciate you pointing that out, @mmcsm. While we always strive for accuracy, we're glad you still enjoyed the film and the story we shared!

comments.author: @AliAiash
comments.text: تحياتي لكم جميعا من اليمن السعيد ❤ كيف يمكن لي زيارة موريتانيا ❤

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: تحياتنا لك في اليمن، @AliAiash! لزيارة موريتانيا، نوصيك بالاطلاع على متطلبات التأشيرة الخاصة ببلدك والبحث عن رحلات جوية إلى العاصمة نواكشوط. إنها رحلة تستحق العناء حقاً!

comments.author: @TravelBeyond4K
comments.text: The sheer scale of the Richat Structure cutting through that relentless Sahara sand is absolutely humbling. You can practically feel the dry desert heat and blinding dust just looking at those vast rocky horizons. Nature here is completely unforgiving yet breathtakingly raw.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: That is a beautiful and poetic description of the Sahara's power, @TravelBeyond4K. Capturing that "unforgiving yet breathtaking" nature was our primary goal for this film. Thank you for the insightful feedback!

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It really does feel endless, @BeyondOurPlanet001. Those vast horizons are exactly what make the Mauritanian desert so captivating!

comments.author: @wanderscope_squad
comments.text: they choose this life. and they seem happier than 90% of people in the city🫶

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: It’s a powerful reminder that happiness often comes from simplicity and community rather than material comforts, @wanderscope_squad. Thanks for sharing that perspective!
